Question_text: IRKAM is a company that produces high quality doors for hotels and offices. The company currently uses job production. The Managing Director, Abdul, believes that quality control is important. He is looking for ways to increase productivity. All workers receive on-the-job training. Abdul is thinking of including off-the-job training as well.
Sub_topic: Difference: production vs productivity
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Concept of quality control, implementation

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'productivity'?
What is meant by ‘on-the-job training'?
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage of off-the-job training for IRKAM.
Identify and explain two reasons why quality control might be important to IRKAM.
Over the past three years there has been a large increase in demand for IRKAM's doors. Do you think job production is still the best method of production for IRKAM? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Sunil is a sole trader. He likes owning a small business. His shop sells low price raincoats. Sales vary throughout the year. The market for raincoats is competitive, but as Sunil makes a profit he doesn't think competition is a problem for his business. In order to protect consumers, the Government of Sunil's country has recently introduced new laws to protect consumers.
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Reasons businesses remain small
How profit made
Reasons markets more competitive
Impact of legal controls: misleading promotion, faulty goods

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'profit'?
Identify two factors which could affect demand for Sunil's products.
Identify and explain two reasons why profit is important to small businesses like Sunil's.
Identify and explain one way in which consumer protection laws might affect Sunil's business and one way consumer protection laws might affect his customers.
Do you think the advantages of owning a small business are greater than the disadvantages for Sunil? Justify your answer.

Question_text: The Government of country H is concerned about the effect of business activity on the environment. It wants to encourage sustainable development. To do this, it is planning to introduce laws to encourage environmentally-friendly production methods. A number of businesses will be affected by these new laws. The Government of country H has collected the data shown in Table 1. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the value of the total output produced in a country in one year. The GDP of country H has risen from $625m in 2000 to $825m in 2011. Table 1: Percentage of GDP by different sectors | % of GDP | 2000 | 2011 | |---|---|---| | Primary sector | 35 | 15 | | Secondary sector | 40 | 25 | | Tertiary sector | 25 | 60 |
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity
Sub_topic: Business impact on environment: global warming
Sustainable development, business contribution
Legal controls: pollution
Economic sectors: primary, secondary, tertiary
Impact: employment, inflation, GDP changes

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'tertiary sector'?
What is meant by 'sustainable development'?
Identify and explain two changes between 2000 and 2011 that are shown in Table 1.
Identify and explain three ways a Government could encourage more businesses to set up in its country.
Do you think that all businesses will be affected by the introduction of the new laws to encourage environmentally-friendly production methods? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Rapid Call is a private limited company. It manufactures a range of cell (mobile) phones. The demand for these is increasing. Its products have several special features that are not available from other phone manufacturers. It sells its products directly to retail shops. Rapid Call uses competitive pricing for all products. The Finance Director has been looking at the accounts. A summary is shown in Table 2. In 2011 the gross profit margin was 40%. Table 2: Profit/Loss Account for Rapid Call for year ending 30 April 2012 ($000s) | | Sales | 450 | |---|---|---| | | Cost of Sales | 300 | | | Gross Profit | 150 | | | Overheads | 95 | | | Net Profit | 55 |
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'private limited company'?
Calculate the gross profit margin for the year ending 30 April 2012.
Identify and explain two ways in which Rapid Call's Finance Director could use the information in Table 2.
The Marketing Director is thinking about changing the channel of distribution. Identify and explain three factors that Rapid Call should consider when choosing a suitable channel of distribution.
How important is increased competition in influencing the marketing strategy of Rapid Call? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Favell is a woodworker. He is planning to set up his own woodworking business. He plans to use marketing to help his business become established in the local area. Favell thinks cash flow will be a problem because his business will have a lot of cash outflows. A friend has suggested he prepares a cash flow forecast.
Sub_topic: What is cash-flow forecast, construction, importance
Role: identifying needs
Characteristics of successful entrepreneurs

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'marketing'?
Identify two possible cash outflows for Favell's business.
Identify and explain two benefits for any business of preparing a cash flow forecast.
Favell is looking at various methods of promotion for his business. Identify and explain three suitable methods of promotion that Favell could use to attract customers.

Favell needs $10000 to buy a motor vehicle so that he can carry all his equipment. He is planning to ask the bank for an overdraft. Do you think this is the most suitable source of finance for him to choose? Justify your answer.
